questions.question: Motion is best defined as
options: a force causing movement of a body
a property of all objects at rest
questions.explanation: Motion is the change in position of an object with time. It is not a force, a property of rest, or a scalar.

questions.question: Oscillatory motion is characterised by
options: motion along a curved path only
questions.explanation: Oscillatory motion is to-and-fro motion about a fixed point (equilibrium). A curved path is not necessary; random and rotational are different types.

questions.question: Rotational motion occurs
questions.explanation: Rotational motion is motion about a fixed axis. A curved path is general, to-and-fro is oscillatory, irregular is random.

questions.question: Distance is a scalar because
options: it is measured only in metres
questions.explanation: A scalar has magnitude only, no direction. Distance is scalar because it does not specify direction.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of speed is
questions.explanation: Speed is distance ÷ time, so the SI unit is metres per second (m/s). B is metre, C is second, D is acceleration.

questions.question: Average velocity is
options: total path divided by total time
questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement ÷ time. B is average speed, C is acceleration, D is average speed.

questions.question: Velocity is a vector because
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude (speed) and direction. B is scalar, C is distance, D is false.

questions.question: Average acceleration is
questions.explanation: Average acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time interval. B is speed, C is velocity, D is not acceleration.

questions.question: The slope of a displacement-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Slope of displacement-time graph = change in displacement ÷ change in time = velocity. B is slope of velocity-time, C is distance, D is speed (magnitude of velocity).

questions.question: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Slope of velocity-time graph = change in velocity ÷ change in time = acceleration. B is area, C is average speed, D is position.

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Area under velocity-time graph = velocity × time = displacement. B is slope, C is average speed, D is time.

questions.question: In a displacement-time graph, displacement is plotted on the
questions.explanation: By convention, displacement (dependent variable) is on the y-axis, time on the x-axis.

questions.question: In a velocity-time graph, time is plotted on the
questions.explanation: Time is the independent variable, plotted on the x-axis.

questions.question: Uniform motion means
questions.explanation: Uniform motion means constant velocity (both speed and direction). B is non-uniform, C is rest, D is non-uniform acceleration.

questions.question: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion are valid when
questions.explanation: The kinematic equations apply only when acceleration is constant. B is rest, C is random, D is circular motion.

questions.question: Free fall is motion under
questions.explanation: Free fall is motion under gravity alone, with air resistance neglected. B, C, D are other forces.

questions.question: For a body released from rest, the downward direction is usually taken as
questions.explanation: By convention, downward is often taken as positive for falling bodies. B would be upward, C is zero, D is undefined.

questions.question: For upward motion under gravity, acceleration is taken as
questions.explanation: If upward is positive, acceleration due to gravity is downward, so a = −g. B would be downward positive, C is no acceleration, D is speed.

questions.question: In free-fall equations, g represents
options: instantaneous speed of the falling body
total vertical height of the body
total time taken by the body
questions.explanation: g is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s²). B is speed, C is height, D is time.

questions.question: For a body released from rest, the initial velocity is
questions.explanation: Released from rest means initial velocity u = 0. B is maximum speed, C is acceleration, D is negative velocity.

questions.question: A body thrown upwards reaches maximum height when its velocity is
questions.explanation: At maximum height, the vertical velocity is momentarily zero before reversing. B is initial, C is acceleration, D is on the way down.

questions.question: The slope of a displacement-time graph for a stationary body is
questions.explanation: A stationary body has constant displacement, so the graph is horizontal; slope = 0. B, C, D are non-zero slopes.

questions.question: Displacement depends on
options: total distance travelled by the body
questions.explanation: Displacement = final position − initial position, so it depends only on initial and final positions. B is distance, C is speed, D is incomplete.

questions.question: Which quantity is scalar?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only (scalar). Velocity, displacement, and acceleration are vectors.

questions.question: Which quantity is vector?
questions.explanation: Acceleration has magnitude and direction (vector). B, C, D are scalars.

questions.question: The total distance in a velocity-time graph is found from the
questions.explanation: Area under velocity-time graph = displacement (or distance if velocity is always positive). Slope gives acceleration.

questions.question: The acceleration in a velocity-time graph is found from the
questions.explanation: Slope of velocity-time graph = acceleration. Area gives displacement.

questions.question: If a velocity-time graph is horizontal, acceleration is
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity-time graph means velocity is constant, so acceleration is zero.

questions.question: If a displacement-time graph is horizontal, velocity is
questions.explanation: Horizontal displacement-time graph means displacement is constant, so velocity is zero.

questions.question: The equations of motion are for motion along a
questions.explanation: The kinematic equations for uniform acceleration apply to straight-line motion. B, C, D are not straight lines.
